newsitem.title: USA: White House braces for court ruling on Internet porn.
newsitem.headline: White House braces for court ruling on Internet porn.

text.p: The White House said Monday that it had not changed its stance on restricting the availability of pornography to children on the Internet, but was weighing what to do if the Supreme Court strikes down a law that limits such access.

"Our administration views are those that we've argued in front of the court," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters. "We want to look ... at ways that we can help families that want to protect kids from smut and indecency."

But McCurry said the White House was studying what to do if the Supreme Court strikes down a 1996 law that makes it a crime punishable by two years in prison and a $250,000 fine to transmit such material on the Internet in a manner available to minors.
He was commenting on a New York Times report published Monday that suggested that the White House was preparing a new policy undercutting its strong support of the law until now.
McCurry said the White House wanted to keep pornographic material away from children, adding: "We're figuring out how to do that depending on what the court might rule."
